subject: Mathematics
source: Original supplementary learning draft aligned to Class 6 Ganita Prakash Chapter 8 (fegp108.pdf), Reprint 2026–27. Verify any school-specific edition before publication.
goals: Use a ruler and compass carefully.
Construct line segments of a specified length.
Copy a line segment and compare lengths.
Understand why arcs and intersections can locate points precisely.
summary: Geometric constructions use tools such as a ruler, compass and protractor to create figures accurately. A construction is not merely a sketch: each line or arc should follow a stated geometric condition.

concepts.title: Construction versus drawing
concepts.explanation: A freehand sketch communicates an approximate shape. A construction uses defined tools and steps to satisfy a mathematical condition accurately.
concepts.example: If a segment must be 5 cm, measure it with a ruler rather than estimating by eye.

concepts.title: Compass as a distance tool
concepts.explanation: A compass keeps a chosen distance between its point and pencil. That distance can be transferred or used to draw an arc from a fixed point.
concepts.example: Set the compass opening to the length AB, then use the same opening to mark an equal length from point P.

concepts.title: Copying a segment
concepts.explanation: Measure or set the compass opening to the original segment, mark a starting point on a ray, and transfer the distance to locate the second endpoint.
concepts.example: If AB is the given length and P is the start, mark Q so PQ = AB.

concepts.title: Accuracy and checking
concepts.explanation: Use sharp pencil marks, steady compass placement and clearly labelled points. Check the result against the given condition instead of judging appearance alone.
concepts.example: A copied segment should match the original length even if it is drawn in a different direction.

workedExamples.question: Construct a segment of length 4 cm using a ruler.
steps: Place the ruler’s zero mark at A and mark B at 4 cm.
Draw the segment AB and label its length.

workedExamples.question: Copy a given segment AB using a compass.
steps: Open the compass to the distance AB.
Draw a ray starting at P.
Without changing the compass opening, place its point at P and mark Q on the ray.

practice.question: Why is a compass useful in copying a length?
practice.answer: It transfers a fixed distance without needing to estimate the length again.
practice.why: The opening stays constant during the transfer.

practice.question: What is the difference between a sketch and a construction?
practice.answer: A sketch is approximate; a construction follows precise tool-based steps to meet a condition.

practice.question: If the compass opening changes while transferring a segment, what happens?
practice.answer: The new segment may not equal the original length.

practice.question: Name two habits that improve construction accuracy.
practice.answer: Use a sharp pencil and stable tool placement; label points clearly and check the required condition.

mcqs.why: A compass maintains a set opening.

mcqs.why: The opening transfers the required length.

questions.q: Explain how a compass can copy a segment.
questions.answer: Set the compass to the original segment length, place its point at the new starting point on a ray, and mark the endpoint without changing the opening.

questions.q: Why is a construction more than a neat drawing?
questions.answer: It follows precise geometric conditions and reproducible steps.

questions.q: Give two ways to reduce errors in a construction.
questions.answer: Keep tools steady, use a sharp pencil, preserve compass opening, label points and check lengths.
